How do I rotate my API key? I think mine leaked in a CI log.

[[retrieved chunks · fetched for message 1]]

[api-keys §2 · score 0.91]
To rotate a key, open Console → Settings → API Keys and click "Rotate". A new key is issued immediately; the old key remains valid for a 15-minute grace window, then is revoked. Rotation does not change your plan, quota, or usage counters. Each organization may hold at most 5 active keys; rotation replaces a key in place and does not consume a slot.

[api-keys §4 · score 0.86]
If a key is exposed publicly (a repository, CI logs, a client-side bundle), rotate it immediately and audit the usage dashboard for unfamiliar traffic. Nimbus continuously scans public GitHub repositories for key patterns and may pre-emptively suspend exposed keys; suspended keys appear with a red badge in Console.

[security §1 · score 0.79]
API keys are displayed exactly once, at creation time. Nimbus stores only a salted hash of each key; support staff cannot recover a lost key under any circumstances — rotation is the only recovery path. Treat keys as secrets: environment variables or a secrets manager, never source control.

assistantBlocks.text:
[[assistant answer 1]]
Rotate it right away: Console → Settings → API Keys → "Rotate" [api-keys §2]. The old key keeps working for a 15-minute grace window, then is revoked [api-keys §2]. Since it leaked in CI, also audit the usage dashboard for unfamiliar traffic — Nimbus scans public repos and may suspend exposed keys on its own [api-keys §4]. One caution: the new key is shown exactly once and support cannot recover it, so store it in a secrets manager this time [security §1].

[rate-limits §1 · score 0.88]
Plans meter requests per calendar month per ORGANIZATION, not per key. Free: 10,000 calls/month. Pro: 1,000,000 calls/month. Burst ceiling on all plans: 50 requests/second. Monthly counters reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st.

[api-keys §2 · score 0.84]
To rotate a key, open Console → Settings → API Keys and click "Rotate". A new key is issued immediately; the old key remains valid for a 15-minute grace window, then is revoked. Rotation does not change your plan, quota, or usage counters.

[rate-limits §3 · score 0.77]
Requests over quota receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Repeatedly exceeding the burst ceiling within a 24-hour window may trigger a temporary key-level throttle; rotating the key does NOT clear an active throttle.

assistantBlocks.text:

No — quotas are metered per organization per calendar month, not per key [rate-limits §1], and rotation explicitly does not change your usage counters [api-keys §2]. One related caution: if you've been hitting the 50 req/s burst ceiling, that throttle is key-level and rotating will not clear it [rate-limits §3].

[auth-troubleshooting §1 · score 0.93]
A 401 immediately after rotation almost always means a cached old key: check environment variables, serverless secret stores, and CDN edge configurations. After the 15-minute grace window the old key returns 401 with error code key_revoked in the response body.

[auth-troubleshooting §2 · score 0.85]
To verify which key a request actually used, read the x-nimbus-key-id response header and compare it against the short ids listed in Console → Settings → API Keys.

[sdk-config §5 · score 0.74]
The Node and Python SDKs read NIMBUS_API_KEY once at process start. Long-lived workers, daemons, and serverless containers with warm instances must be restarted or redeployed to pick up a rotated key.

assistantBlocks.text:
[[assistant answer 3]]
A 401 right after rotating almost always means something is still sending the OLD key — once the 15-minute grace window ends it returns 401 with code key_revoked [auth-troubleshooting §1]. Check environment variables, serverless secret stores, and CDN edge configs, and restart any long-lived workers — the SDKs only read NIMBUS_API_KEY at process start [sdk-config §5]. To confirm which key a request is actually using, compare the x-nimbus-key-id response header against Console → API Keys [auth-troubleshooting §2].
